statement: For boosted trees and XGBoost, early stopping on a stopping set of a tenth of the fit's units (patience 20 or 50, up to 1,000 or 2,000 rounds) chooses the number of trees well once the plan's effective size is at least 1,500, so that the stopping set inside an inner fit holds about 100 or more units of the rarest class; below 1,500, searching the number of trees directly is better.
regime: prediction; boosted_trees, xgboost Sobol candidates; n_plan >= 1,500 (ES on) or < 1,500 (trees searched)
decision: early-stopping switch of the Sobol candidates; stopping-set share
user_sees: Boosted trees' methods text: "Searched settings stop early from an effective size of 1,500 ... holding back a tenth of the fold's units, the latest when the folds follow time."
claimed_basis: RECIPES §4.2 'Early stopping' and 'Stopping set' rows (no citation); §4.1 table (patience 20 / 50, rounds 1,000 / 2,000).
notes: [part id F1-007] STOP_SHARE = 0.1 at tuning.py:97; switch decided at :953. Arithmetic: 1,500 x 2/3 (K = 3) x 1/10 = 100. For a numeric outcome the 'rarest class' rationale does not apply but the same 1,500 threshold is used. [Merged F4-006 at turbotab/core/models/boosted_trees.py:77; its basis: RECIPES §4.1–4.2 (stopping set sized so it holds ~100+ units of the rarest class); patience values: none stated.; its notes: Also xgboost_family.py:70-71 (STOP_ROUNDS 2,000, PATIENCE 50) and :508-510. scikit-learn's own n_iter_no_change default is 10, so 20 is TurboTab's; no source for 20 or 50. The 1,500 threshold is tuning.py's (other fork). XGBoost stopped boosters are truncated to best_iteration+1 (xgboost_family.py:304).]

statement: Complementary-pairs stability selection with B = 50 pairs of random halves, each half's first q variables on the lasso path, threshold tau = 0.6 and q = floor(sqrt((2*tau - 1)*p)) keeps the expected number of falsely selected predictors at or below 1 (Meinshausen & Bühlmann's bound q^2/((2*tau - 1)p), which complementary pairs keep under the same exchangeability assumption).
regime: prediction; numeric or yes/no outcome; selection method = stability
user_sees: "stability selection with complementary pairs (Shah & Samworth 2013; 50 pairs of halves, threshold 0.6) kept a short reproducible panel"; label 'controls false selections, not prediction error'
claimed_basis: Meinshausen & Bühlmann 2010 Thm 1; Shah & Samworth 2013 (JRSS B 75:55); tau = 'the lower end of Meinshausen & Bühlmann's (0.6, 0.9)' (variable_selection.py:57-59).
notes: [part id F3-012] The known-truth test uses B=25, p=60, n=200, 15 independent sparse datasets. q is floored at 1, so for p < 5 the bound exceeds 1 (p=3: 1/(0.2*3)=1.67), contradicting 'chosen so the bound is one'. For a yes/no outcome the base procedure is least-squares LARS on 0/1 (lasso_first), not a logistic lasso. Selection is per column then lifted to terms (any column kept keeps the term), which can raise false term selections above the column-level bound. The bound needs exchangeability and a better-than-random base procedure, which correlated nutrition predictors may violate.

statement: A regression-calibrated coefficient's interval must come from a bootstrap over the whole chain (resampling PSUs within strata, whole clusters, or people as the design says, and re-imputing each resample 5 times under multiple imputation); model-based intervals and Rubin's rules over each copy's model-based variance are too narrow and are refused.
decision: refusal of model_based and rubin_only intervals; how the interval is computed
user_sees: "A calibrated coefficient's model-based interval treats E[X | W̄, Z] as measured: 'one cannot use the usual model standard errors ... as these will be too small' (Keogh et al. 2020, §6.1.2)."
claimed_basis: Keogh, Shaw & Gustafson 2020 §6.1.2; Schomaker & Heumann (Boot MI); Rao & Wu (PSU bootstrap); MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 7.
notes: [part id F5-032] The simulation (200 datasets of 300, 100 resamples) shows Boot MI coverage >= 0.93 and Rubin-only < 0.90 in one setting; the survey PSU branch is checked for mechanism only (test_4_the_bootstrap_draws_whole_psus_within_strata_as_rao_and_wu_do).

statement: Open noticings must be given their dispositions before the plan's lock under Estimate and Describe (and under an unanswered purpose), or before the held-out rows open under Predict; a disposition recorded after that point would be chosen with the numbers in view, so the triage is refused and each noticing is decided on its own as made after the estimates or held-out scores were seen.
regime: All purposes; gate = plan lock (Estimate, Describe, unanswered) or seal opened (Predict)
decision: Whether 'Confirm all' on the open-noticings triage is accepted
user_sees: "The open noticings are triaged before the plan is fixed, and that has happened: each is decided on its own now, as made after the estimates were seen."
claimed_basis: calm/FOUNDATION §7; UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §7 ruling 1 as re-ruled 2026-10-09 (module docstring); no literature cited
notes: [part id F6-016] Also sweep.py:461-470 (gate_stage, gate_passed). Under Predict the gate is the seal, not the first cross-validated score, so dispositions chosen after CV scores were seen are accepted as pre-gate; the implicit claim is that this leaves the held-out score honest. test_confirm_sweep.py::test_the_triage_is_confirmed_only_before_its_gate_passes pins behavior.

statement: For clustering, a column with exactly two distinct values (e.g. a 0/1 code) is a category, not an amount.
user_sees: Same refusal as for categories, naming the two-valued column.

statement: A per-protocol result must be reported beside the intention-to-treat result, never alone.
user_sees: A per-protocol result is reported beside the intention-to-treat result, never instead of it.

statement: An exclusion rule that reads the outcome (its column, ranges set by it, or any input of a Goldberg screen that is the outcome) selects on the value being explained and biases the estimates, so it is refused in each sensitivity analysis as in the primary.
user_sees: A rule reads the outcome `bmi`. Keeping rows by their outcome selects on the value being explained, which biases the estimates, and no one whose outcome is still unknown could be screened by it.
notes: OUTCOME_RULE text lives in turbotab/core/decisions.py:3804 (other slice; possible duplicate). Merged duplicate: methods/misreporting.py:27-29 cites Banna et al. 2017 ('body weight is included in both the calculation of implausible rEI and the outcome variable … which could artificially elevate the association'); the |r| >= 0.5 warning for a correlated outcome is S6-070.

statement: sd(r_i)/√n_sim over the simulated units' final risks bounds the g-formula's Monte Carlo error from above.
decision: the methods text's Monte Carlo error
notes: With n_sim equal to the units, sd(r_i) includes between-unit variation, so it is an upper bound; with a resampled base it is about the Monte Carlo SE itself. The sentence reports the larger of always and never (stages/time_varying.py:1026).

statement: An infinite value, typically a ratio over a zero denominator (such as protein per 1,000 kcal on a day recorded as 0 kcal), is not a measurement, and setting it to missing is the repair.
user_sees: "An infinite value is not a measurement: no mean, model or plot can use it." Option "Set to missing".
notes: The 0-kcal day behind the value may be a recording error or a real non-intake day. Blanking the cell sends it to the missing-values answer, which treats it as missing at random. | Inventory source id: F2-038.

statement: A nutrient recorded as a percent of energy carries no constant kcal per unit, so a substitution cannot move energy through it by a factor and must use the share-of-energy scale instead; a column recorded in a non-food unit (lb, cm, years) is no amount of food energy and is refused.
decision: Refusal of a kcal-factor substitution on a %-energy or non-food-unit column.
user_sees: "`col` is recorded as a share of energy, which carries no constant kcal per unit" with route "Move a share of energy instead (the substitution's share-of-energy scale)"
claimed_basis: None stated beyond the docstring's reasoning.
notes: Low-risk logical claim. | Inventory source id: F3-030.

statement: Under the genomics or metabolomics lens, a block of at least 20 numeric non-outcome, non-identifier, non-acquisition columns is unnormalized (needs a normalization before modeling) if, for counts, at least 20 of them are non-negative whole numbers with more than two distinct values reaching a maximum of at least 100 (genomics lens), or, for intensities, they are non-negative and their positive values span at least 100-fold and either reach at least 1,000 or have median per-feature skewness of at least 0.5 (metabolomics lens); values failing these tests are treated as already normalized or log-scale.
regime: genomics or metabolomics lens; >=20 assay-like numeric columns; read from values only, outcome never consulted, before the split
decision: whether the omics_scale finding is raised, which arms the refusal of linear families and the normalization question
user_sees: Finding: "`N` columns hold raw counts, and library sizes differ by sample." / "... hold raw intensities, and total signal differs by sample." with repair options to normalize
claimed_basis: Constants commented in code (omics.py:64-68): 'log2 intensities stay below ~40', 'raw intensities reach thousands', 'unlogged concentrations are right-skewed (a log-normal feature with a 30% CV has skewness near 1); log-scale ones are not'; genotype dosages 0/1/2 excluded by COUNT_MAX. No citation.
notes: The test is a known-label check on 8 repo sample files (raw counts, CPM, TMM-CPM, VST, microarray, untargeted raw, logged) plus genotype dosages; it would catch gross misreading but does not validate the thresholds generally (e.g., a log-scale block with values >=1000 after a scaling, or right-skewed log values). The finding is the gate for F5 entries on refusal and normalization. Constants at omics.py:64-68; _median_skew at :200. | Inventory source id: F5-001.

statement: Adjusting for total energy does not by itself make a substitution isocaloric: the swapped components must be measured and analyzed in calories, and with components in grams or servings the substitution reported is not the one intended.
regime: dietary lens; substitution between two exposures
decision: whether a substitution is offered (two energy-bearing exposures required) and its unit
user_sees: Adjusting for total energy does not by itself make a substitution isocaloric. The components must be measured and analyzed in calories; in grams or servings, the substitution reported is not the …
notes: Also why 1219-1222 ('grams and servings do not make an isocaloric swap'), term 1236-1237, interview.py:313. For macronutrients in grams with energy held fixed, a coefficient is still an isocaloric swap per gram (e.g., 1 g fat = 9 kcal of the rest), so grams change the scale rather than the isocaloric property; the claim holds for gram-for-gram swaps of sources with different energy density and for servings. The Estimate beats state swaps in grams ('25 g more sugar, 25 g less other carbohydrate').

statement: On a food-frequency questionnaire a blank frequently means 'never', especially among older participants, so that missingness is not at random, and standard multiple imputation, which assumes it is, is an improvement but not a solution.
user_sees: On a food-frequency questionnaire a blank frequently means never, especially among older participants. That missingness is not at random, and standard multiple imputation assumes it is: an …
notes: 'An improvement' over what is unstated (complete cases?). Quest noticing diet-ffq-blank-means-never.

statement: When a time-varying confounder was itself affected by earlier exposure, standard regression is biased whether it adjusts for that confounder or not, while marginal structural models with inverse-probability weights or the parametric g-formula adjust for it at each time point; stabilized weights should average near 1.
regime: inference; exposure varying within units over time points
user_sees: standard regression is biased either way: adjusting for it removes part of the effect, and leaving it out leaves the later values confounded (Robins, Hernán & Brumback 2000).
notes: Terms 1531-1536. A mean near 1 is necessary, not sufficient (Cole & Hernán).

statement: For a least-squares estimate on an outcome with a clinical cut-off c, writing y = min(y, c) + max(y − c, 0) splits the coefficient exactly into a part from values above the cut and a part from values below, which add to the primary's coefficient, and the estimate is 'mostly the tail' when the part above is more than half and its interval excludes zero.
regime: inference; linear model; outcome with a clinical cut-off
decision: the 'typical person, or the tail?' standing question
user_sees: "The typical person, or the tail?" "Mostly the tail: the diabetic range."
claimed_basis: linearity of least squares in y (no source)
notes: The additivity is exact for OLS. 'From values in the diabetic range' attributes the part to people above the cut, but it is the clipped excess above c among everyone.
